notes: HOMOGRAPH NOTE: two adjacent LOC entries stand in the left column. (a) 'ickawiir(a)-' LOC 'raised upward.' <ickawiira, cf. SB ickaweera-, Ar. iskaweera- upward>, example haakickawiirat; (b) 'ickawiira-' LOC '1. upstream. 2. westward, in a westerly direction.', transcribed here because its bold headword matches the work-list headword exactly. Etymology names one underlying form followed by cf. cognates (no + or .), so I classed it as analysis with a single piece; no literal translation is printed ('upward' glosses the SB/Ar. cognates), hence literal null and meaning unknown. Second gloss: 'westward, in a westerly direction.' Examples: ickawiiraʔat 'go upstream; go west.'; ickawiiraʔa (ir...) 'come upstream; come west.' (the second example is broken across lines as 'ickawiira-' / 'ʔa (ir...)').

Two homographs in the left column: 'icusawask' VI(1) {dist., icusawaawask} 'smile, grin, as when laughing to oneself; snicker, titter.' <icus+awask, nose to laugh>, and 'icusawask (ut...)' VT(1), transcribed here because the work list gives class VT. The reading ut = 'at' comes from comparing the two etymologies on this page (the VI literal is 'nose to laugh'; the VT literal adds 'at'). Forms 3 and 5 are broken across lines ('tuuticusa-' / 'waskuʔ'; 'tuuticusawas-' / 'kista') and joined.

In the literal translation the first part is the Pawnee form 'kaatu' itself, printed untranslated in the sans-serif Pawnee type; so the page gives no English meaning for that piece.
